QF.id: AIFM CIII AIFs in India and Suitability_9

question.text: Kaveri Macro Fund is launching its first scheme as a Category III AIF. The fund manager is finalising the PPM. Which pair of thresholds is CORRECT?

answer.text: Minimum corpus INR 10 crore; minimum investor ticket INR 50 lakh
Minimum corpus INR 20 crore; minimum investor ticket INR 1 crore (INR 25 lakh for employees)
Minimum corpus INR 100 crore; minimum investor ticket INR 5 crore
Minimum corpus INR 50 crore; minimum investor ticket INR 25 lakh for all investors

explanation.text: The Logic: Tables 4.2, 4.3 and 4.4 consistently state: Cat III AIF minimum corpus is INR 20 crore; minimum investor ticket is INR 1 crore (INR 25 lakh for employees of the AIF; not applicable to Accredited Investors). These are SEBI (AIF) Regulations core eligibility thresholds. The Trap: Option A puts PMS's INR 50 lakh ticket on an AIF. Option C inflates the numbers. Option D forgets the INR 1 crore ticket applies to non-employees. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A through XIX-E all test the INR 20 cr / INR 1 cr pair. In XIX-E (Manager), you must also track the employee carve-out and the Accredited Investor exemption for corpus compliance reporting. Manager's Pro-Tip: Before first closing, confirm each investor's subscription agreement has executed drawdown for at least INR 1 crore (or INR 25 lakh + employee attestation). SEBI's first-close audit checks subscription documents; a single sub-1-crore non-employee subscriber can derail the scheme.
